newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rally again boosted by bond market.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rally again boosted by bond market.

text.p: Stocks rolled to another record Tuesday, boosted by a strong performance in the bond market that sent interest rates to their lowest levels in nearly eight months.

The Dow Jones industrial average rose 53.42 points to 8,174.53, the second consecutive record for the blue-chip average and the fifth in the last six sessions. Several other broader market gauges also set records.
Interest-rate sensitive stocks paced the rally, with banks and other financial companies and those dependent on economic cycles posting the strongest advances.

Investors got a double dose of good news to start the session -- the bipartisan deal reached late on Monday to balance the federal budget and a government report on Tuesday showing that labour costs rose 0.8 percent in the second quarter, in line with private economists' forecasts.

Bond market investors especially liked the reports since they pointed to low inflation. The 30-year Treasury rose a quarter point and its yield, which moves in the opposite direction from the price, fell to 6.39 percent from 6.40 percent Monday. It was the lowest yield on the benchmark bond since Dec. 3.

"If you're looking for a story in stocks today, bonds are the story," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "The budget deal helped and the data showed the economic backdrop remains the same -- sugar sweet."

"Money just seems to be pouring into the rate-sensitive financials and cyclicals," said Guy Truicko, portfolio manager at Unity Management. "Right now, investors seem to be delighted with the economic environment."
Investors still face some major economic reports this week, including the first reading of the economy's second-quarter performance, due Thursday, and the monthly jobs report for July, due Friday.
Analysts said that with the corporate earnings season drawing near an end, investors' focus would probably shift back toward bonds and interest rates in coming weeks.

Rate-sensitive stocks paced Tuesday's rally, with American Express Co. rising 3-9/16 to 82-7/16, the biggest rise among the 30 Dow components. J.P. Morgan & Co. added 3-1/2 to 114-1/4 and Caterpillar climbed 2-3/16 to 59-3/4.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,691 to 1,120 on active volume of about 545 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Among individual issues, Citicorp jumped 4-7/8 to 129 after Merrill Lynch raised its rating on the stock.

Cyrix Corp. gained 1-7/8 to 24-15/16 after announcing late Monday that it agreed to be acquired by National Semiconductor Corp. for $550 million in stock. National Semiconductor shares fell two to 31.
PLC Systems tumbled 12-3/16 to 13-5/16 after a Food and Drug Administration panel recommended that the FDA reject the company's laser system for treating certain heart conditions.
Galileo Technology jumped 10-1/4 to 27-1/4 in the semiconductor company's first session after its initial public offering.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks rose 5.84 points to 942.29, a record.
The Nasdaq composite index, laden with high-technology issues, rose 8.79 points to 1,572.32.
The NYSE composite rose 2.50 points to 488.43, a record.
The average price per share gained 23 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues, also known as the Wilshire 5,000 -- ended at a record 8,913.604, up 45.670, or 0.52 percent.
